2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, in short, are that the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2, as plaintiff, instituted Title Suit No. 220 of 1999 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Sylhet for declaration of title in respect of the land described in Schedule No. 1 and further declaration that two registered deeds described in Schedule No. 3 are illegal, ineffective, concocted and not binding upon the plaintiffs, stating that the suit land measuring an area of 1-47 acres appertaining to Plot Nos. 1051 and 1052 under SA Khatian Nos. 171 and 225 respectively, originally belonged to one Rash Moni Das alias Rash Ram Das and Bishnu Charan Das and their names stood recorded in khatian in equal share. Rash Ram Das died leaving behind two sons namely, Umesh Chandra Das and Promesh Chandra Das and they became owners of half of the land i.e. 0.73½ acre. While they were in possession of the same, sold out 0.47 acre land to one Farmuz Ali, predecessor of the plaintiffs and proforma-defendant No. 4, by a registered deed of sale dated 5-6-1970, Said Farmuz Ali while in possession of the same sold out the whole 47 decimals of land to one Abdur Rob by a registered deed of sale dated 21-4-1980 and said Abdur Rob while in enjoyment sold out the same to the plaintiffs and the proforma defendant No. 4 by a registered deed of sale dated 5-7-1987. Said Bishnu Charan Das while in possession sold out his entire share i.e. 73½ decimals of land to the plaintiffs and the proforma defendant No. 4 by a registered deed of sale dated 13-12-1988. Said Umesh Chandra Das and Promesh Chandra Das thereafter sold their remaining 26½ decimals of land to one Yogya Ram Das who got possession and enjoyed the same. Thereafter, Yogya Ram Das sold out 3½ decimals of land therefrom to the plaintiffs and defendant No. 4 by a registered deed of sale dated 15-2-1989 and sold out the rest 23 decimals to Mohesh Chandra Das and Mohim Chandra Das who sold out the same to Nobo Kumar Das by a registered deed of sale dated 1-4-1998. Against the said transfer the plaintiffs filed Pre-emption Case No. 15 of 1998 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Kanaighat, Sylhet which was allowed in favour of the preemptors i.e. the plaintiffs. In the aforesaid way the plaintiffs and proforma-defendant No. 4 has acquired title in the whole 1.47 acres of land of the suit plots and they have been possessing the same. The defendant No. 1 has no right, title or interest in the suit land. Nevertheless, the defendant No. 1 has created 2(two) registered deeds by which Mohesh Chandra and Mohim Chandra transferred 39 decimals of land in favour of the defendant No. 1. Those two deeds have also clouded the title of the plaintiffs, as such, the plaintiffs have become compelled to file the instant suit. 

 8. As admitted by the parties, suit plot Nos. 1051 and 1052 measuring 1-47 sataks belonged to Rash Ram Das and Bishnu Charan Das in equal share measuring 73 1/2 sataks each. Rash Ram Das died leaving 2(two) sons, Umesh Chandra Das and Promesh Chandra Das who transferred 47 sataks of land to one Farmuz Ali, father of plaintiffs, by a sale deed dated 5-6-1970 (Exhibit 3). Farmuz Ali subsequently, transferred the same to one Abdur Rob by a registered deed dated 22-4-1980 (Exhibit 4). The plaintiffs claim that they purchased the said property from Abdur Rob by a sale deed dated 5-7-1987 (Exhibit 1(Ka). Said Deed No. 5161 dated 5-07-1987 in original has been filed by the plaintiffs which shows that they purchased 15 sataks of land from Plot No. 1051 under Khatian No. 172 and 32 sataks from Plot No. 1228 under Khatian No. 238 and by the said deed no property was purchased by them from Plot No. 1052. However, said Plot No. 1052 contains in the deed of Abdur Rob dated 22-4-1980 (Exhibit 4). After transfer to Farmuz Ali, Umesh and Promesh had 26 1/2 sataks of land which was transferred to one Yogya Ram Das as admitted by the parties but neither the plaintiffs nor the defendant filed any deed in the name of Yogya Ram Das. Said Yogya Ram Das by a sale deed dated 15-2-1989 Exhibit 6(kha) transferred 3¼ sataks of land to the plaintiffs and proforma-defendant No. 4 the rest 23 sataks of land also transferred by him to Mohesh Chandra and Mohim Chandra but no such deed has been submitted by the parties to the proceedings. Mohesh and Mohim by a sale Deed No. 2151 of 1998 dated 1-4-1998 (Exhibit Ga) transferred the same to one Nabo Kumar Das. Before the said transfer Mohesh and Mohim Chandra by 2(two) Registered Deed Nos. 2223 of 1998 and 2218 of 1998 both executed on 26-3-1998 and registered on 5-4-1998 transferred 39 sataks of land to the defendant No. 1 (Exhibits-6 and 6(Ka). 

 10. From the documents available in file, it appears that the plaintiffs purchased 73½ sataks of land from Bishnu Charan Das by sale deed dated 13-12-1988 (Exhibit 2), 15 sataks of land in Plot No. 1051 under Khatian No. 172 from Abdur Rob by deed dated 5-7-1987 (Exhibit l(Ka) and 3¼ sataks of land from Plot Nos. 1051 and 1052 and also claim that they got 23 sataks of land by preemption in Preemption Case No. 15 of 1998. 

 14. As stated above, the plaintiffs and proforma-defendant No. 4 acquired (73½ + 15 + 3) = 91.75 sataks of land by deed dated 13-12-1988, 5-7-1987 and 15-2-1989 Exhibits-2, 1(Ka) and 6(Kha) respectively, from Plot Nos. 1051 and 1052, In Preemption Case No. 15 of 1998 though preemption was allowed in favour of plaintiffs but the deed of Nabo Kumar dated 1-4-1998 being executed later than the deed dated 26-3-1998 of the defendant No. 1, by the said deed neither Nabo Kumar nor the plaintiffs acquired any title. Therefore, said 23 sataks of land shall cover by the deeds executed by Mohim and Mohesh on 26-3-1998 in favour of defendant No. 1. In the schedule to the original Deed No. 5161 executed by Abdur Rob in favour of me plaintiffs and proforma-defendant No. 4, Plot No. 1052 is totally absent but certified copy of the same contains Plot No. 1052, Khatian No. 225 measuring 32 sataks (Exhibits 1 and 1(Ka). Learned Lawyer for the opposite-parties could not satisfy the court why there is such anomalies in the 2(two) deeds. However, by the documentary evidences available in file vendor of the defendant No. 1 by purchase from Yogya Ram Das acquired 23 sataks of land in the suit plots but they transferred 39 sataks of land from 2(two) plots in favour of defendant No. 1 by 2(two) separate deeds dated 26-3-1998 and in favour of Nabo Kumar by deed dated 1-4-1998 measuring 23 sataks totalling 62 sataks, where they have only title in 23 sataks and the same was transferred firstly, to the defendant No. 1 and secondly, to Nabo Kumar. Since the deed in favour of defendant No. 1-petitioner was executed earlier by Mohim and Mohesh and admitting the said deed the plaintiff-opposite-parties filed Preemption Case No. 19 of 1998 seeking preemption of the same but ultimately foiled, the defendant No. 1 acquired title in Plot Nos. 1051 and 1052 for 23 sataks only.
